newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank bonds salesmen go to Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank bonds salesmen go to Deutsche.

text.p: Five bond salesman have defected from Commerzbank AG to join rival Deutsche Bank AG in London and Frankfurt, the banks said on Monday.
Four of Commerzbank's seven-strong Frankfurt sales team for domestic bonds are leaving to join Deutsche, a Commerzbank spokesman said. A fifth is moving to Deutsche in London.
They are specialists in the sale of domestic bonds to institutional investors. The moves would in no way paralyse Commerzbank's business in the area, the spokesman said.
One of the Frankfurt salesman leaving is Kurt Ebert. The others were not named.

In its bid to become a world player, Deutsche has embarked on a high-profile recruitment drive and has been accused by rivals of luring staff with "telephone number" pay packages, a charge it has denied.
At one point earlier this year Deutsche was threatened with court action for poaching by rival ING Barings.
But Deutsche and Commerzbank sought to play down the latest move, saying such transfers were common among banks.
"We're happy about this increase, evidently Deutsche Bank is an attractive place for good people," Deutsche spokesman Detlev Rahmsdorf said. "Staff movements between banks are normal and frequent."
But while this is not the first team defection in the Frankfurt banking scene, migration here is far less common than on the big battlegrounds of investment banking like London.

Market contacts are regarded as the principal asset of investment bankers. People with the right contacts are at an advantage in clinching lucrative business for their banks in the placement of big share and bond issues.
